a continuous objective and feasible constraints on $X\times Z$ represented by finite factorable expression DAGs, tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, positive integer node budget $N$, a verified interval/relaxation rule table, and deterministic verified bound oracles. Every relaxation rule must meet [[alg-factorable-mccormick-box-relaxation]], and every bound used for pruning or a gap certificate must meet [[thm-factorable-dual-certificate-is-valid-box-lower-bound]] on a nonempty feasible node. The integer set $Z$ is finite by boundedness of every coordinate interval. Every main-tree node evaluation consumes one unit of the budget and each oracle call returns in finite time or gives an explicit unavailable status.

A main-tree node is $(J,B)$, where $J$ is a product of bounded integer intervals and $B\subseteq X$ is a continuous box. Relax each integer interval to its real hull and construct the node relaxation with [[alg-factorable-mccormick-box-relaxation]]; when it supplies a verified dual lower bound, its validity on the original integer-feasible node is covered by [[thm-factorable-dual-certificate-is-valid-box-lower-bound]]. The oracle may also return a feasible witness with a verified objective upper bound, an emptiness proof, or an unavailable status. The latter never supplies a finite lower bound. Store lower bounds for all nonempty terminal nodes; prune only certified-empty nodes, and close a node only when its lower bound is at least $U-\varepsilon$, retaining that bound in the global ledger.

Input a positive integer $n$, a nonempty complex matrix family $\mathcal M$ enclosed entrywise by finite dyadic real/imaginary rectangles, a dyadic center matrix $M_0$, a certified dyadic bound $\delta_A\ge\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}\|M-M_0\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$, and a simple positively oriented strictly convex polygon $\Gamma$ with dyadic vertices and filled interior $P$. Supply the dyadic disk cover and point preconditioners required by [[alg-complex-resolvent-cover-validator]], a positive integer $N$ for midpoint subdivisions of each edge, a positive integer $K_\pi$ for the arctangent series, and a finite arithmetic budget. The family may be the monodromy block of a validated shooting jet; no correlation between matrix entries is required. A complex rectangle here is the product of one closed dyadic real interval and one closed dyadic imaginary interval for each matrix entry.

Input a box $B\subseteq D_0$, a finite real expression DAG from [[def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls]] using addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, a precision schedule $p\ge2$, and a dyadic format with fixed exponent bounds. The DAG must define a real-valued function at every point of $B$; for each division node its denominator range on $B$ must exclude zero. Traverse the finite DAG in topological order. Enclose each input by its interval in $B$, each exact constant by a certified interval, and apply the corresponding outward-rounded operation from [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] at precision $p$. Return the root enclosure $I_p(B)=[a_-,a_+]$, its lower and upper endpoints, and the exact midpoint of $B$ as a candidate point. If any operation returns overflow, split-domain, domain-error, entire, or inconclusive, return that status with no finite bound claim.

Let $m_j=(a_j+b_j)/2$ and $r=\max_j(b_j-a_j)/2$. Use [[alg-interval-dag-box-enclosure-and-bound]] at the singleton $\{m\}$ to obtain $I_p(\{m\})=[q_-,q_+]$. Compute a directed-rounding upper bound $r^+\ge r$ and a downward-rounded lower endpoint $\ell_B\le q_- - Lr^+$. Return the lower-bound report $\ell_B$ and the feasible midpoint candidate $(m,q_+)$. If either interval or arithmetic calculation is non-finite, return inconclusive.

Input an exact rational $q$, a target $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, and a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$. The target value is $w=e^{\pi iq}=\cos(\pi q)+i\sin(\pi q)$ by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], for the canonical Fourier $\pi$ identified with the interval evaluator's constant by [[thm-na-interval-pi-matches-canonical-fourier-pi]]. For precision $p=p_0,p_0+1,\ldots,p_{\max}$, build the finite expression DAG for $\cos(\pi q)$ and $\sin(\pi q)$, with rational constants enclosed by directed dyadic rounding, and call [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] using the dyadic format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$ and truncation index $J$; its fixed finite-cell rules govern range reduction. If either result is non-finite, continue at the next precision unless the precision cap is reached, in which case return `inconclusive` with the supplier status. If the results are finite intervals $C=[c_-,c_+]$ and $S=[s_-,s_+]$, set $\widehat w=c_-+is_-$ and compute an upward-rounded dyadic $\epsilon\ge(c_+-c_-)+(s_+-s_-)$. If $\epsilon\le\tau$, return `certified(\widehat w,\epsilon)`; otherwise continue or return `inconclusive` at the cap. A non-finite endpoint or overflow returns its explicit failure status. The routine makes no finite-error claim on a failure branch.

3. If $N$ is composite and not a power of two, find its least divisor $r$ with $1<r<N$ by trial division and put $s=N/r$. For $u=0,\ldots,r-1$, recursively call this procedure with the same controls on the strided vector $(x_{u+rv})_{v=0}^{s-1}$ to obtain an approximate unnormalised length-$s$ DFT $U_u$. For each $0\le k_2<s$ and $0\le u<r$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-2uk_2/N$ to obtain the twiddle enclosure, then multiply its returned phase by $U_u(k_2)$ using $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}$. Apply this procedure recursively, with the same controls, to the resulting vector indexed by $u$ at length $r$. Store its output $k_1$ at index $k_2+sk_1$. Propagate any failed phase or arithmetic status.

4. If $N$ is prime, set $M$ to the least power of two with $M\ge2N-1$. For each $0\le j<N$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-j^2/N$ to obtain $\widehat\alpha_j$, and set $a_j=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\alpha_jx_j)$; set the remaining entries of $a\in\mathbb C^M$ to zero. For each $-(N-1)\le t\le N-1$, obtain $\widehat\beta_t$ by the same call with $q=t^2/N$ and set $b_{[t]_M}=\widehat\beta_t$, setting other entries of $b$ to zero. Compute the cyclic convolution with [[alg-na-computed-fft-cyclic-and-linear-convolution]] in `cyclic` mode using controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. For each $0\le k<N$, obtain $\widehat\gamma_k$ by the same phase call with $q=-k^2/N$ and set $\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\gamma_k\widehat c_k)$. Return the first $N$ entries or the first failure status.

Input real numbers $a<b$, a natural $n\ge0$, sampled values $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, and the phase/FFT controls for [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]]: a phase tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. Set $m=(a+b)/2$ and $d=(b-a)/2$. For an underlying $f\in C[a,b]$, admissible samples satisfy $y_0=f(m)$ when $n=0$ and $y_j=f(m+d\cos(\iota(j)\pi/\iota(n)))$ for $0\le j\le n$ when $n\ge1$, using the canonical real images of [[def-canonical-natural]]. The output is an approximate real quadrature value or the first status returned by the called DFT procedure.

2. If $n\ge1$, form $z\in\mathbb C^{2n}$ by $z_j:=y_j+0i$ for $0\le j\le n$ and $z_{2n-j}:=y_j+0i$ for $1\le j<n$. This is the even extension $(y_0,\ldots,y_n,y_{n-1},\ldots,y_1)$, with real samples embedded as complex numbers with zero imaginary part. Call [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] on $z$ with length $2n$ and the same controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. If it returns a status instead of a vector, return that status.

For direction `forward`, at $N=1$ return $x_0$. For $N>1$, if $d_{\max}=0$ return `inconclusive` with the `subdivision-cap-exhausted` status. Otherwise split $x$ into even and odd subsequences and recursively compute their unitary transforms $E,O$ by calling this routine with the same phase parameters and depth cap $d_{\max}-1$. For each $0\le k<N/2$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-2k/N$, obtaining $(\widehat w_k,\epsilon_k)$ approximating $w_k=e^{-2\pi ik/N}$. Compute the six-real-operation complex product $t_k=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat w_kO_k)$, componentwise rounded sums $s_k^+=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(E_k+t_k)$ and $s_k^-=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(E_k-t_k)$, and $\widehat c=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{1/2})$. Set output entries $k$ and $k+N/2$ to the componentwise rounded real scalings $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat c s_k^+)$ and $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat c s_k^-)$, respectively. For direction `inverse`, conjugate the input, run the forward routine with the same phase parameters and $d_{\max}$, and conjugate its output; conjugation is exact in the operationwise model. Propagate any failed phase certificate; on arithmetic failure return the operationwise range status and index. Accuracy is asserted only by the separate theorem and only on a successful no-range-failure execution.

For either mode, call [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] on each length-$M$ input with direction `forward` and the same $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$ controls. Multiply corresponding transform entries as $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat A_k\widehat B_k)$ using the six-real-operation complex product of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Call the same FFT routine on this product vector with direction `inverse` and the same controls, and multiply each output component by the computed real scalar $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt M)$ using componentwise rounded real scaling. Return the length-$M$ cyclic result, or its first $L$ entries in linear mode, only if every phase, recursion-budget, and arithmetic operation succeeds; otherwise return the first `inconclusive` or `range-failure` status and index. The exact convolution identity and numerical-error claim are separate results.

**Independent validation:** run [[alg-krawczyk-root-certification]] on $F$ and $Z$ with $C,W,\eta$ and the supplied box budget. First its exact check $WC=I$ must succeed. For every processed subbox $Y\subseteq Z$, let $m_Y$ be its rational midpoint. The residual callback runs the validated shooting jet on $\{m_Y\}$ and returns its $F(m_Y)$ enclosure as $F_0$; the Jacobian callback runs it on $Y$ and returns its $DF(Y)$ enclosure as $J(Y)$. Both append the sound outward section-row enclosures in section mode. This uses the actual midpoint of the current Krawczyk box, even when it differs from the candidate center. A failed query or tube inclusion marks that box unresolved. All interval operations are outward under [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. Retain only a box $Y$ with strict Krawczyk inclusion and its separately certified contraction bound below one. Over its physical-state projection $X_Y$ (over $X_Y\times\Lambda_Y$ in section mode), use the supplied field range query to require at least one component interval excluding zero. Finally require a successful full-box jet run on $Y$ to enclose the entire trajectory and monodromy; a failed query or tube check returns inconclusive.

At a certified root, a tangent routine must certify a unit vector in $\ker DF$ and a rank-$d+1$ condition. The predictor is advanced along that tangent. The corrector is [[alg-validated-periodic-orbit-corrector]] in section mode, which appends the pseudo-arclength plane and validates the resulting square residual by Krawczyk inclusion. Forward its complete finite input package: the candidate mode and its required pointwise evaluators if that mode uses them (or choose its enclosure-guided mode), rational initial candidate and validation box, validated-jet step counts and arithmetic caps, preconditioner and exact inverse witness, minimum Krawczyk box width, and box/update budgets. For possibly nonrational tangent/predictor data, forward certified outward rational enclosures of the affine section row and its derivative; unavailable row bounds return inconclusive. The arithmetic evaluator supplies exact or interval-enclosed $F$ and $DF$ from the validated shooting jet. The local inverse and chart interfaces are [[lem-phase-bordered-shooting-jacobian-invertibility]] and [[thm-pseudo-arclength-local-newton-correction]]. Run [[alg-pseudo-arclength-continuation-with-certified-local-corrector]] with these callbacks and its chart, angle, inverse, and finite-budget checks.

For every outgoing guard, apply [[alg-smooth-function-root-isolation]] to the exact reference guard $h(t)=g(t,y_{\rm ref}(t))$ over the new trial interval, using its certified range and derivative enclosures and box budget $B_{\mathrm{root}}$. If any isolator is `inconclusive` or has unresolved boxes, return `inconclusive`. For each certified root box, classify the crossing using its derivative enclosure and the guard's declared orientation. A box strictly on the opposite side is nontriggering; a box whose derivative enclosure meets zero is refined or makes the result `inconclusive`.

For a rational box $Q=X\times\Lambda\times\Theta$ with $\Theta\subset(0,\infty)$, a **validated shooting jet enclosure** consists of: (i) a box containing $P\Phi_\theta(q)$ for every $q,\theta$ in the input; (ii) a box containing the residual $G(Q)$; (iii) an interval matrix $J(Q)$ containing every $DG(q,\theta)$; and (iv) trajectory and monodromy boxes containing every scaled trajectory $P\Phi_{\theta s}(q)$, $0\le s\le1$, and the physical-state block of $\mathcal M$. The boxes use [[def-real-boxes-and-interval-jacobian-enclosures]] and [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. The exact derivative formula follows from [[prop-shooting-residual-derivative]], and its flow sensitivity is on the common tube of [[lem-c1-ode-flow-on-common-tube]]. A finite success record is admissible only when obtained by the range-oracle procedure of [[alg-validated-euler-flow-and-monodromy-enclosure]], whose exact flow and monodromy enclosure is guaranteed by [[thm-validated-euler-flow-and-monodromy-enclosure-soundness]], with all queries and interval operations successful and outward under [[def-verified-flow-variational-range-oracle]]. In particular, to enclose the period column the procedure requests $H^\#$ on an endpoint box $X_T\times\{I\}\times\Theta\subseteq K$ and divides its physical field block by the positive interval $\Theta$. Any unavailable query or inclusion returns inconclusive. A finite Newton, multiple-shooting, or collocation residual alone is not a validated jet enclosure.
